title: Does the hanger a sim loop designs change for stretchy, heavy knits, and what does a tee-designed hanger cost them?
lede: does the hanger that `hanger-fit`'s CMA-ES designs change for stretchy, heavy knits? The best arm width moves from +0.9 cm past the half shoulder (tee) to +1.5–1.8 cm (EA 40 N/m), but slope, bow and end radius are not pinned down at 150 scores; a tee hanger scores 1.06 cm on a soft double-weight knit against 0.52 cm for one designed for it. Fabric constants swept, not measured.
summary: Runs hanger-fit's CMA-ES and random-search design loop (150 scores, 3 seeds) on five size M cases taken from hanger-sweep's corners: base tee, stiff (EA 800), soft (EA 40), soft and double weight, and soft, double weight on a 10 cm strip. The best arm half-width is 0.9 cm past the half shoulder for the tee and 1.5–1.8 cm for the stretchy cases, but slope, bow and end radius scatter between seeds at similar error, so only the width is identified. A tee-designed hanger scores 0.22 cm RMS on the tee and 1.06 cm on the soft heavy knit; one designed for the knit scores 0.52 and 0.76 cm. CMA-ES beats random search in all five cases. The narrow-strip case is poor for every hanger (best 0.99 cm). Fabric constants are swept corners, not measurements; 2D model, one size, shape error only.
